items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 13 at 2:59PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
ESFAFC

Locations:

* Willow and Talkeetna
* Rivers, creeks, and streams with headwaters along the western
Talkeetna Mountains

Timing:

* Monday evening through Wednesday afternoon. Heaviest rainfall
expected through Tuesday evening.

Rainfall:

* Rainfall totals of 1 to 3 inches Monday through Wednesday likely
won't be high enough for widespread flooding, but smaller
tributaries draining the Talkeetnas including Willow Creek and the
Little Susitna will likely reach bankfull.

Hydrologic Concer

items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 13 at 12:09PM AKDT until September 15 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...
Kwigillingok, Kongiganak, and Kipnuk: Water levels as
high as 1.0 to 2.5 feet above the normal highest tide line.
Southwest winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts to 40 to 45 mph before
winds transition to west Tuesday morning, diminishing impacts.

Toksook Bay and Tununak: West winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts to
45 to 50 mph beginning Tuesday morning. Water levels as high as
0.5 to 1.5 feet above the normal highest tide line.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kwigillingok,
Kongiganak,
items.areas: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
items.instruction:

items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 13 at 11:44AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Lower Koyukuk Valley-Lower Yukon and Innoko Valleys-Lower Yukon
River-Middle Yukon Valley

Heavy rain is forecast to begin Monday afternoon. Rain should
continue through Wednesday morning with storm total rainfall of up to
2 inches expected. With already saturated ground conditions across
the region, the heavy rain may cause minor pooling/ponding of water
beginning on Tuesday.

Mainstem river flooding is not expected, but high water levels and
bankfull conditions

items.description:

expected.
